troponin_i_hs_abbott.origin: The 99th-percentile limits are manufacturer values derived by a robust statistic from 1,531 apparently healthy participants aged 21 to 75 years (764 women, 766 men); troponin was measurable in 78% of the women [S5]. An independent re-derivation in the American Association for Clinical Chemistry (AACC) Universal Sample Bank (340 healthy women after exclusions) gave a lower female 99th percentile of 13 ng/L, with troponin measurable in 42% of women, and showed that stricter health exclusions lowered the limit [S6].
troponin_i_hs_abbott.sexSpecificWhat: 99th-percentile upper reference limit defining myocardial injury; the thresholds used in the High-STEACS trial
troponin_i_hs_abbott.contestedSummary: With a single contemporary-assay threshold, type 1 myocardial infarction (MI) was diagnosed in 11% of women and 19% of men; with the high-sensitivity assay and sex-specific thresholds, in 22% of women and 21% of men. Of the 56 reclassified women, 25% had died or had a reinfarction at 12 months and 2% underwent angiography [S1]. In the High-STEACS trial (48,282 patients), 1,470 of 1,771 reclassified patients (83%) were women and myocardial injury in women increased by 42% (3,521 to 4,991), but MI or cardiovascular death at 1 year in reclassified patients was not reduced (15% versus 12%; adjusted odds ratio 1.10, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.61) [S2][S3]. In England in 2019, 54 of 97 trusts reporting a threshold used sex-specific thresholds [S7].
troponin_i_hs_abbott.guidanceInBand: The Fourth Universal Definition states that “Detection of an elevated cTn value above the 99th percentile URL is defined as myocardial injury” and that “sex-specific 99th percentile URLs are recommended for hs-cTn assays”; acute myocardial infarction additionally requires “a rising and/or falling pattern of cTn values with at least one value above the 99th percentile URL” with evidence of ischaemia [S4].
troponin_i_hs_abbott.labRangeSource: Abbott ARCHITECT STAT High Sensitive Troponin-I package insert (outside the US, April 2015), as tabulated by IFCC C-CB v05/2023; the US insert (September 2019) gives 17, 35 and 28 ng/L (female, male, overall)

troponin_t_hs_roche.origin: Roche’s EU 99th-percentile limits (overall 14, women 9, men 17 ng/L) were derived from 533 participants aged 20 to 71 years, with troponin measurable in 49.7% of the women; the US Gen 5 values (19, 14 and 22 ng/L respectively) were derived from 1,301 participants aged 21 to 89 years [S5]. In the American Association for Clinical Chemistry (AACC) Universal Sample Bank, high-sensitivity troponin T was measurable in 16 to 21% of healthy women and the female 99th percentile was 10 to 11 ng/L [S6]. Outside the US, most laboratories use the single 14 ng/L limit [S6][S8].
troponin_t_hs_roche.sexSpecificWhat: 99th-percentile upper reference limit defining myocardial injury (EU package insert; the US Gen 5 insert gives 14 and 22 ng/L)
troponin_t_hs_roche.contestedSummary: The Fourth Universal Definition recommends sex-specific 99th percentiles for all high-sensitivity assays [S4], but Roche released only a combined 14 ng/L threshold outside the US; in an international survey, 12 of 12 institutions using high-sensitivity troponin T applied the combined value, whereas 5 of 6 using high-sensitivity troponin I applied sex-specific thresholds [S8]. In England, where the Roche assay was used in 57% of trusts, 54 of 97 trusts reporting a threshold used sex-specific values in 2019 [S7]. The High-STEACS outcome evidence [S1][S2][S3] was generated with the Abbott assay, not the Roche assay.
troponin_t_hs_roche.guidanceInBand: The Fourth Universal Definition states that “Significantly lower values are observed among women compared with men” and that “sex-specific 99th percentile URLs are recommended for hs-cTn assays”, while noting that “there is controversy as to whether this approach provides valuable additional information” [S4].
troponin_t_hs_roche.labRangeSource: University of Iowa Hospitals pathology handbook (Roche US 5th-generation hs-TnT; same values as the Roche US Gen 5 package insert in the IFCC table). The EU insert gives 9, 17 and 14 ng/L (female, male, overall); NHS Lothian reports 1 to 9 ng/L (female) and 1 to 16 ng/L (male)

troponin_i_hs_siemens.origin: The manufacturer’s 99th percentiles were derived non-parametrically from 2,001 participants aged 22 to 91 years (1,007 women, 994 men); 62% of women had values measurable above the limit of detection [S5]. Re-derivation in the Universal Sample Bank gave 38, 44 and 26 ng/L (overall, men, women) for the Atellica assay [S6]. Siemens values are numerically higher than those of other assays because the assays are not harmonised; a value is interpretable only against the limit of its own assay [S6].
troponin_i_hs_siemens.sexSpecificWhat: 99th-percentile upper reference limit defining myocardial injury
troponin_i_hs_siemens.contestedSummary: No outcome trial equivalent to High-STEACS exists for this assay; the case for sex-specific limits rests on the general recommendation of the Fourth Universal Definition [S4] and on the consistently lower female distribution (26 versus 44 ng/L in the sample bank) [S6].
troponin_i_hs_siemens.guidanceInBand: The Fourth Universal Definition states that “sex-specific 99th percentile URLs are recommended for hs-cTn assays” [S4] and that the 99th percentile “must be determined for each specific assay” [S4].
troponin_i_hs_siemens.labRangeSource: Siemens Atellica High-Sensitivity TnI package insert (FDA 510(k), July 2018), as tabulated by IFCC C-CB v05/2023; ADVIA Centaur: 39.6, 58.0 and 46.5 ng/L (female, male, overall)

troponin_i_hs_beckman.origin: The manufacturer’s 99th percentiles were derived non-parametrically from 1,089 participants aged 21 to 99 years (595 women, 494 men) [S5]. In the Universal Sample Bank, 48% of healthy women had measurable values, the robust female 99th percentile could not be computed, and the non-parametric values were 18, 18 and 20 ng/L (overall, men, women) [S6].
troponin_i_hs_beckman.sexSpecificWhat: 99th-percentile upper reference limit defining myocardial injury
troponin_i_hs_beckman.contestedSummary: The female limit is defined from a population in which fewer than half of the women had a measurable result, which the authors of the Clinical Chemistry study stated disqualifies the assay from high-sensitivity status for women [S6]; a footnote to the International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (IFCC) table cautions that manufacturers may list assays that do not meet the criterion of ≥50% measurable results in both sexes [S5]. No sex-specific outcome trial exists for this assay.
troponin_i_hs_beckman.guidanceInBand: The Fourth Universal Definition states that “sex-specific 99th percentile URLs are recommended for hs-cTn assays” [S4] and that a high-sensitivity assay should “measure cTn values above the assay's LoD in ≥ 50% of healthy individuals” [S4].
troponin_i_hs_beckman.labRangeSource: Beckman Coulter Access 2 hsTnI package insert (US, lithium heparin plasma, June 2018), as tabulated by IFCC C-CB v05/2023

creatinine.origin: Labcorp attributes its sex-partitioned interval only to “Labcorp internal studies”, with no population or year stated [S11]; ARUP publishes no interval (“By report”) [S12]. Creatinine production depends on muscle mass: in 170 healthy adults, lean mass predicted serum creatinine but not cystatin C [S16]. The eGFR equation encodes sex with κ = 0.7 (female) versus 0.9 (male), α = −0.241 versus −0.302, and a multiplier of 1.012 for women; it was fitted on 8,254 participants (43.7% female) [S14][S15].
creatinine.sexSpecificWhat: CKD-EPI 2021 female sex multiplier (with sex-specific κ 0.7/0.9 and α −0.241/−0.302, female/male) in the eGFR equation
creatinine.contestedSummary: In a woman with low muscle mass, creatinine may lie within the female reference interval (0.57 to 1.00 mg/dL) while filtration is reduced, because creatinine reflects muscle mass as well as GFR [S16]; the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) 2024 guideline names “reduced muscle mass” as a reason to prefer cystatin C-based eGFR [S17]. The female interval itself is documented only as “internal studies” [S11]. No study quantifying under-detection of chronic kidney disease in women attributable to the female interval was identified.
creatinine.guidanceInBand: The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline states: “We recommend using eGFRcr-cys in clinical situations when eGFRcr is less accurate and GFR affects clinical decision-making (1C)” and “Consider eGFRcys rather than eGFRcr-cys in otherwise healthy populations with decreased creatinine generation due to reduced muscle mass” [S17].
creatinine.labRangeSource: Labcorp test 001370 (kinetic Jaffe), ages ≥15 years; attributed to “Labcorp internal studies”

nt_probnp.origin: The 125 pg/mL rule-out threshold is the value stated by the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) as the “upper limit of normal in the non-acute setting” [S19], a single value for both sexes. Healthy-population data show higher values in women at every age: in 18,356 participants in Scotland without cardiovascular disease, median (97.5th percentile) NT-proBNP under 30 years of age was 51 (196) pg/mL in women and 21 (104) pg/mL in men [S20]. Sex-partitioned hospital reference intervals (for example, Iowa) therefore give women a higher upper limit than men [S18].
nt_probnp.sexSpecificWhat: No guideline sex-specific threshold; the ESC applies NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL (BNP <35 pg/mL) to all adults
nt_probnp.contestedSummary: NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/mL was present in 9.8% of healthy women and 1.4% of men under 30 years of age (adjusted odds ratio for women 9.48, 95% CI 5.60 to 16.1); the authors stated that “An NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/mL is common in females without classical cardiovascular risk factors” and called for age- and sex-specific thresholds [S20]. In the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study, absolute risk at guideline thresholds was lower in White women and higher in Black men [S21]. The direction of misclassification is over-identification of healthy women, the opposite of that for troponin.
nt_probnp.guidanceInBand: The European Society of Cardiology (ESC) states that “A plasma concentration of … NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL … make a diagnosis of HF unlikely”; above this value echocardiography is advised, with the caveat that elevated natriuretic peptides have causes including “AF, increasing age, and acute or chronic kidney disease” [S19].
nt_probnp.labRangeSource: University of Iowa Hospitals pathology handbook, ages 19 to 44 years (95th percentiles in patients without congestive heart failure; rising with age: women 65 to 74 years 0 to 353 pg/mL, men 65 to 74 years 0 to 229 pg/mL); the value for both sexes is the ESC 2021 non-acute upper limit of normal

creatine_kinase.origin: Labcorp states no provenance for its CK intervals [S22]. Population-derived 97.5th percentiles are higher: 207 U/L in women in the Tromsø Study (n = 6,904 after exclusions) [S23]; 295 U/L in white women and 487 U/L in Black women in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011 to 2014 (n = 10,096) [S25]. In Amsterdam, limits were 2 to 5 times the manufacturer’s, and 49% of participants of African descent exceeded the manufacturer’s limits [S24].
creatine_kinase.sexSpecificWhat: Laboratory upper reference limit (Labcorp, ages 18 to 50 years); no guideline-set sex-specific threshold exists
creatine_kinase.contestedSummary: Each population study cited places the female 97.5th percentile above the 182 U/L laboratory limit: 207 U/L in Norway [S23], and 295 U/L in white and 487 U/L in Black US women [S25]. Ancestry has a larger effect than sex partitioning accounts for: odds ratios for elevated CK were 5.08 in Black women and 8.39 in Black men, and body composition did not explain the difference [S25]; in Amsterdam, 49% of participants of African descent exceeded the manufacturer’s limit [S24].
creatine_kinase.guidanceInBand: No society guideline statement on sex-specific interpretation of CK was identified. The authors of the Amsterdam study concluded that “The variation in CK activity within the population is wider than previously suggested” and that raising the upper reference limit “may improve the use of statins” [S24].
creatine_kinase.labRangeSource: Labcorp test 001362, ages 18 to 50 years (kinetic, 340 nm); no source cited

uric_acid.origin: Labcorp attributes the male interval to internal studies and cites no source for the female interval [S27]. The disease thresholds have a different origin: urate crystallises above its saturation point, and the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) defines asymptomatic hyperuricaemia “as an SU concentration of ≥6.8 mg/dl” (SU, serum urate) [S28]; treatment targets of <6 mg/dL (ACR; European League Against Rheumatism, EULAR) are set below saturation so that crystals dissolve [S28][S29].
uric_acid.sexSpecificWhat: No sex-specific guideline threshold: the ACR and EULAR targets (<6 mg/dL; EULAR <5 mg/dL in severe gout) and the ≥6.8 mg/dL definition of hyperuricaemia apply to both sexes; only laboratory reference intervals are sex-partitioned
uric_acid.contestedSummary: The female laboratory interval is a population distribution, not a risk threshold, and for older women (upper limits 7.2 and 7.9 mg/dL) it extends above both the 6 mg/dL treatment target and the 6.8 mg/dL saturation-based definition of hyperuricaemia [S27][S28]. In the Framingham cohort (2,476 women; 104 incident gout cases among them), gout risk in women rose in a graded manner with urate, although less steeply than in men [S30]. The American College of Rheumatology (ACR) notes that “Gout has differential impact on patients by sex”, but its patient panel comprised eight men [S28].
uric_acid.guidanceInBand: The American College of Rheumatology (ACR) states that “Initiating ULT is conditionally recommended against in patients with asymptomatic hyperuricemia” (≥6.8 mg/dL without flares or tophi); for diagnosed gout, “we strongly recommend continuing ULT to achieve and maintain an SU target of <6 mg/dl over no target” [S28]. The European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) target is “<6 mg/dL (360 µmol/L) and <5 mg/dL (300 µmol/L) in those with severe gout” [S29]. ULT denotes urate-lowering therapy; SU, serum urate.
uric_acid.labRangeSource: Labcorp test 001057 (uricase): female ages 18 to 50 years (51 to 70 years: 3.0 to 7.2 mg/dL; ≥71 years: 3.1 to 7.9 mg/dL), male ages ≥18 years; male interval attributed to “LabCorp internal studies”, female interval unattributed
